title: Theosophy
author: Rudolf Steiner (1910 trans)
description: Theosophy: An Introduction to the Supersensible Knowledge of the World and the Destination of Man by Rudolf Steiner (Theosophie, 1904), in an early English translation (1910). One of Steiner's four basic books, written while he was General Secretary of the German Theosophical Society, it presents his spiritual-scientific understanding of the human being. Part one describes the threefold nature of the human being as body, soul and spirit and its ninefold subdivision (physical, etheric and astral bodies, the sentient, intellectual and consciousness souls, and spirit-self, life-spirit and spirit-man). Part two explains reincarnation and karma as the destiny of the spirit. Part three describes the three worlds, the physical, the soul world and the spirit land (devachan), and the path of the soul through them after death. A closing chapter outlines the path of knowledge by which anyone may verify these teachings. It is a foundational text of Anthroposophy.
